cases.review_disclosure: Synthetic examples authored by Codex. Any factual rubric scores are Codex-assisted operator judgments, not independent human subject-matter validation.
cases.business_question: Can a small model draft concise replies that preserve supplied facts and avoid promises it cannot support?
cases.conclusion: The disclosed factual review improved from 4 to 7 acceptable replies out of 12. Correct original answers were credited even when they echoed the message. The trained model better preserved the written-approval and inspection requirements, but invented a repair deadline and recommended a video upload despite a text-only policy. The deadline error failed a critical test. This candidate remains below target and must not send unsupervised customer replies. Its separate fresh-input check also omitted the missing-address request and review step.

cases.name: Action summaries
cases.rubric: Pass if the output preserves the agreed action, owner and deadline with the three labelled fields in order. Semantically equivalent concise action wording is allowed. Missing information must be not stated, tentative suggestions must not become commitments, and contradictory agreements must return review. Fail for invented responsibility or dates.
cases.scope: Turn notes into a factual action, owner and deadline. Synthetic English text only. Review-assisted demonstration, not production or customer validation. The reserved cases are fixed before the first run. Reusing them after a model change makes them development evidence.
